title: Boundary disputes - revenue records vs a court decree
p1:
A land map says one thing. A court order says another. So which one actually decides the boundary?

Many property owners are surprised when the document they trusted for years does not settle the dispute.
p2:
A common misconception is that revenue records automatically prove ownership and exact boundaries. They are useful government records, but they mainly help with land administration and taxation.

A court decree, after a proper legal process, carries a different weight because it is a judicial determination of rights.
p3:
In simple terms, revenue records can show what is recorded in official registers, but they do not always decide a contested boundary. When there is a conflict, a final court decree can become the stronger reference point for determining legal rights.

The practical lesson: before buying land or relying on old records, check whether any court decision affects the property. A small boundary issue today can become a major dispute tomorrow.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a property dispute where government records and a court order pointed in different directions? Which document do you think most people misunderstand?
